# Utility (4 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /endpoints | `platform`?, `search`?, `method`? | 0 | List every available endpoint |
| /endpoint | `id` / `url` | 0 | How to use any endpoint |
| /quickstart | `platform`? | 0 | Get started in one call |
| /llms | `platform`?, `format`? | 0 | AI-agent context payload |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /endpoints — 0cr

Machine-readable catalog of every active SocialCrawl endpoint: path, method, platform, credit cost, required and optional parameters, response archetype, and a link to the per-endpoint usage guide. Generated from the endpoint registry at request time, so it never drifts from what is callable. Free to call.

**Parameters**

- `platform` *(optional)*: Filter the catalog to a single platform slug (e.g. tiktok)
- `search` *(optional)*: Case-insensitive substring filter over endpoint paths and summaries
- `method` *(optional)*: Filter by HTTP method

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/utility/endpoints" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /endpoint — 0cr

Complete usage guide for a single endpoint: every parameter with type, description and example, the exact credit cost, cache behaviour, pagination recipe, a copy-paste example request, an example response, the response schema URL, and related endpoints. Identify the endpoint by id (tiktok/profile) or url (/v1/tiktok/profile). Free to call.

**Parameters**

- `method` *(optional)*: Disambiguates resources registered under more than one HTTP method
- `id` / `url` — at least one required.
  - `id`: Endpoint id as platform/resource, e.g. tiktok/profile (one of: id, url — at least one required)
  - `url`: Endpoint path form, e.g. /v1/tiktok/profile (a full https URL also works) (one of: id, url — at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/utility/endpoint?id=<id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /quickstart — 0cr

Everything needed for a first successful API call in one response: authentication, base URL, the response envelope, the credit billing model, the error taxonomy, rate limits, pagination rules, and a copy-paste first request. Pass platform to tailor the first-call example. Free to call.

**Parameters**

- `platform` *(optional)*: Tailor the first-call example and links to one platform slug

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/utility/quickstart" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /llms — 0cr

The SocialCrawl context corpus for AI agents, served through the API: the same content as llms.txt for the whole API or a single platform, as markdown or structured JSON. An agent with an API key can bootstrap itself with one call instead of scraping documentation pages. Free to call.

**Parameters**

- `platform` *(optional)*: Scope the context to one platform slug
- `format` *(optional)*: markdown (default) returns the llms corpus text; json returns a structured context object

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/utility/llms" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### Use these before assuming the catalogue

The plugin's reference files are generated from a **committed snapshot**, so they describe the
API as of the snapshot date. The live catalogue has moved on every occasion it has been
checked. When a call 404s, or when the user asks about an endpoint the refs do not list,
`/endpoints` (0cr) settles it against the live API for free — always cheaper than guessing or
than a failed paid call.

`/endpoint` (0cr) returns usage for a single path, which is the fastest way to confirm a
parameter name before spending credits on a call that would 400.
